ids.sargon-of-akkad: A gardener's foster son who became the first emperor in history.
ids.hammurabi: The king of Babylon who carved his laws in stone for everyone to read.
ids.ramesses-ii: Egypt's showman pharaoh: warrior, builder, and maker of the oldest known peace treaty.
ids.cyrus-the-great: The founder of the Persian Empire, remembered by friends and enemies alike as a just king.
ids.darius-i: The organiser of the Persian Empire, whose royal couriers inspired the US Postal Service's motto.
ids.cleopatra: The last queen of ancient Egypt, who outwitted Rome for twenty years.
ids.pericles: The leader of Athens in its golden age, who built the Parthenon.
ids.socrates: The barefoot questioner of Athens, who chose death over silence.
ids.plato: Socrates' pupil, who founded the Academy and wrote philosophy's most famous books.
ids.aristotle: Alexander the Great's teacher, who wrote about almost everything and founded logic and biology.
ids.alexander-the-great: He conquered an empire from Greece to India before he was 33, and never lost a battle.
ids.hannibal: The Carthaginian general who crossed the Alps with elephants and nearly brought down Rome.
ids.pompey: Rome's greatest general before Caesar, and Caesar's partner, then rival.
ids.julius-caesar: The general who conquered Gaul, crossed the Rubicon, and was stabbed on the Ides of March.
ids.mark-antony: Caesar's right-hand man, Cleopatra's lover, and Octavian's great rival.
ids.augustus: Rome's first emperor, who found the city brick and left it marble.
ids.gautama-buddha: A prince who gave up his palace to find the end of suffering, and woke up.
ids.ashoka: The conqueror who was horrified by his own war and became a king of peace.
ids.confucius: China's great teacher, whose ideas on family and good government shaped East Asia.
ids.qin-shi-huang: The First Emperor, who united China and was buried with an army of clay.
ids.jesus: The teacher from Nazareth whose life and death gave rise to Christianity.
ids.paul-the-apostle: The persecutor turned apostle, who carried Christianity across the Roman world.
ids.marcus-aurelius: The philosopher emperor who wrote notes to himself on how to live.
ids.constantine-the-great: The first Christian emperor, who founded Constantinople.
ids.augustine-of-hippo: The restless young man who became the greatest thinker of the early Church.
ids.attila: The king of the Huns, called the Scourge of God.
ids.justinian-i: The emperor who built Hagia Sophia and wrote down Roman law.
ids.muhammad: The Prophet of Islam, who united Arabia under the faith in one God.
ids.ali: The cousin of the Prophet, fourth caliph of Islam and first imam of the Shia.
ids.saladin: The sultan who won back Jerusalem, admired by friend and foe for his mercy.
ids.charlemagne: The king of the Franks who united western Europe and was crowned emperor in 800.
ids.william-the-conqueror: The Duke of Normandy who won England at the Battle of Hastings in 1066.
ids.marco-polo: The Venetian who served Kublai Khan and told Europe about China.
ids.genghis-khan: An outcast boy of the steppe who built the largest land empire in history.
ids.kublai-khan: The grandson of Genghis Khan who conquered China and built the city that became Beijing.
ids.mansa-musa: The king of Mali whose gold-laden pilgrimage made him a legend.
ids.ibn-battuta: The traveller from Tangier who went farther than anyone before the age of steam.
ids.timur: The lame conqueror of Central Asia, builder of Samarkand and destroyer of cities.
ids.zheng-he: The admiral of the Ming treasure fleets, who sailed to Africa long before Europe did.
ids.joan-of-arc: The peasant girl who led the French army at 17 and was burned at 19.
ids.johannes-gutenberg: The goldsmith of Mainz whose printing press changed the world.
ids.isabella-i-of-castile: The queen who united Spain, conquered Granada and sent Columbus west.
ids.christopher-columbus: The sailor who crossed the Atlantic in 1492, thinking he had reached Asia.
ids.vasco-da-gama: The Portuguese captain who found the sea route from Europe to India.
ids.leonardo-da-vinci: The painter of the Mona Lisa, who filled notebooks with machines no one could yet build.
ids.michelangelo: The sculptor of David and painter of the Sistine Chapel ceiling.
ids.nicolaus-copernicus: The church official who moved the Earth out of the centre of the universe.
ids.martin-luther: The monk whose protest split the Church and started the Reformation.
ids.hernan-cortes: The Spanish adventurer who brought down the Aztec Empire.
ids.ferdinand-magellan: The captain whose fleet was the first to sail around the world.
ids.charles-v-holy-roman-emperor: The emperor who ruled half of Europe and the Americas, then gave it all up.
ids.suleiman-the-magnificent: The sultan who ruled the Ottoman Empire at its height.
ids.francisco-pizarro: The conqueror of the Inca Empire, who could not read or write.
ids.henry-viii: The king of six wives, who broke with Rome to found the Church of England.
ids.akbar: The great Mughal emperor who could not read, and welcomed every religion to his court.
ids.philip-ii-of-spain: The king of Spain at its height, who sent the Armada against England.
ids.elizabeth-i: The Virgin Queen who beat the Armada and gave her name to a golden age.
ids.william-shakespeare: The glover's son from Stratford who became the greatest writer in English.
ids.galileo-galilei: The scientist who turned a telescope on the sky and stood trial for saying the Earth moves.
ids.oliver-cromwell: The farmer turned general who beheaded a king and ruled England as Lord Protector.
ids.louis-xiv: The Sun King, who built Versailles and reigned for 72 years.
ids.isaac-newton: The farm boy who found the rules that move the planets.
ids.peter-the-great: The giant tsar who dragged Russia into the modern world.
ids.aurangzeb: The last great Mughal emperor, who ruled India at its largest.
ids.frederick-the-great: The flute-playing soldier king who made Prussia a great power.
ids.catherine-the-great: The German princess who seized the Russian throne and ruled for 34 years.
ids.james-cook: The farm boy turned navigator who mapped the Pacific.
ids.george-washington: The general who won American independence, then gave up power.
ids.wolfgang-amadeus-mozart: The child prodigy who wrote more than 600 works before he died at 35.
ids.napoleon: The Corsican officer who crowned himself emperor and conquered most of Europe.
ids.simon-bolivar: El Libertador, who freed six South American countries from Spanish rule.
ids.ludwig-van-beethoven: He wrote the world's most famous symphonies, the greatest of them after he had gone deaf.
ids.karl-marx: The thinker whose ideas of class struggle and communism shook the 20th century.
ids.charles-darwin: The naturalist whose voyage on the Beagle led him to the theory of evolution.
ids.queen-victoria: She reigned for 63 years, and gave her name to an age.
ids.abraham-lincoln: Born in a log cabin, he led the United States through its Civil War and ended slavery.
ids.otto-von-bismarck: The Iron Chancellor, who united Germany with "blood and iron".
ids.vladimir-lenin: The revolutionary who led the Russian Revolution and founded the Soviet Union.
ids.joseph-stalin: The dictator who made the Soviet Union a superpower at the cost of millions of lives.
ids.mustafa-kemal-ataturk: The general who founded modern Turkey and remade it from top to bottom.
ids.albert-einstein: The patent clerk who discovered relativity and E = mc², and changed how we see the universe.
ids.marie-curie: The first woman to win a Nobel Prize, and the only person to win in two sciences.
ids.benito-mussolini: The founder of fascism, dictator of Italy and ally of Hitler.
ids.adolf-hitler: The Nazi dictator who started the Second World War in Europe and ordered the Holocaust.
ids.winston-churchill: The prime minister who refused to give in to Hitler, and led Britain through the Second World War.
ids.franklin-d-roosevelt: The president who fought the Great Depression with the New Deal and led America in the Second World War.
ids.mahatma-gandhi: He led India to independence without violence, and inspired the world.
ids.chiang-kai-shek: The Nationalist leader who united China, fought Japan, then lost the mainland to Mao.
ids.mao-zedong: The communist who founded the People's Republic of China, whose campaigns cost tens of millions of lives.
ids.ho-chi-minh: The revolutionary who led Vietnam to independence from France.
ids.deng-xiaoping: The small, tough leader who opened China's economy to the world.
ids.ruhollah-khomeini: The cleric who led the Iranian Revolution and founded the Islamic Republic.
ids.archimedes: The greatest mathematician of the ancient world, who shouted "Eureka!"
ids.euclid: The father of geometry, whose textbook was used for 2,000 years.
ids.pythagoras: The mystery man of numbers, whose theorem every student learns.
ids.aryabhata: The Indian astronomer who said the Earth spins, and helped give the world its numbers.
ids.al-khwarizmi: The scholar of Baghdad who gave us algebra, and whose name became "algorithm".
ids.avicenna: The boy genius of Bukhara whose medical book was used for 600 years.
ids.cai-lun: The court official honoured for giving the world paper.
ids.johannes-kepler: The astronomer who found the laws that move the planets.
ids.rene-descartes: The philosopher who said "I think, therefore I am", and put shapes on a grid.
ids.gottfried-wilhelm-leibniz: The genius who invented calculus, binary numbers and a calculating machine.
ids.antonie-van-leeuwenhoek: The cloth merchant who first saw bacteria through lenses he made himself.
ids.antoine-lavoisier: The father of modern chemistry, who named oxygen and lost his head in the Revolution.
ids.benjamin-franklin: Printer, scientist, inventor and diplomat: the most many-sided of America's founders.
ids.james-watt: The instrument maker whose steam engine powered the Industrial Revolution.
ids.michael-faraday: The bookbinder's boy who discovered how to make electricity from magnetism.
ids.louis-pasteur: The chemist who proved that germs cause disease, and made the first rabies vaccine.
ids.gregor-mendel: The monk whose pea plants revealed the laws of heredity, ignored until after his death.
ids.dmitri-mendeleev: The Siberian chemist who arranged the elements in the periodic table, and left gaps for new ones.
ids.thomas-edison: The inventor of the phonograph and the light bulb, with 1,093 patents to his name.
ids.alexander-graham-bell: The teacher of the deaf who invented the telephone.
ids.nikola-tesla: The genius behind alternating current, radio control and the Tesla coil.
ids.wright-brothers: Two bicycle makers from Ohio who made the first powered airplane flight.
ids.henry-ford: The farm boy who put the world on wheels with the Model T and the assembly line.
ids.sigmund-freud: The Viennese doctor who explored the unconscious mind and invented psychoanalysis.
ids.j-robert-oppenheimer: The physicist who led the making of the first atomic bomb, and then warned the world about it.
ids.alan-turing: The codebreaker who helped win the Second World War and imagined the modern computer.
ids.florence-nightingale: The Lady with the Lamp, who founded modern nursing and fought disease with statistics.
ids.alexander-von-humboldt: The explorer who saw nature as one connected web, and the founder of ecology.
ids.johann-sebastian-bach: The church musician whose music many call the greatest ever written.
ids.richard-wagner: The composer of the Ring, who built his own opera house, and whose music still divides people.
ids.raphael: The painter of grace and harmony, who died at 37 at the height of his fame.
ids.sandro-botticelli: The painter of The Birth of Venus, favourite of the Medici.
ids.rembrandt: The Dutch master of light and shadow, who painted himself nearly 100 times.
ids.johannes-vermeer: The quiet painter of Delft, master of light, who left only about 35 pictures.
ids.vincent-van-gogh: He painted The Starry Night and Sunflowers, and is said to have sold just one painting in his life.
ids.claude-monet: The father of Impressionism, who painted light, haystacks and his water lily pond.
ids.pablo-picasso: The most famous artist of the 20th century, co-founder of Cubism and painter of Guernica.
ids.filippo-brunelleschi: The goldsmith who rediscovered perspective and raised the great dome of Florence.
ids.mimar-sinan: The greatest Ottoman architect, who built over 300 buildings.
ids.dante-alighieri: The exiled poet of Florence who imagined a journey through Hell, Purgatory and Heaven.
ids.miguel-de-cervantes: The soldier, slave and tax collector who wrote Don Quixote.
ids.johann-wolfgang-von-goethe: Germany's greatest writer, author of Faust, who also studied plants, bones and colours.
ids.leo-tolstoy: The count who wrote War and Peace, then tried to live like a peasant and preached non-violence.
ids.charles-dickens: The boy who worked in a factory at 12 and grew up to write Oliver Twist and A Christmas Carol.
ids.victor-hugo: The giant of French writing, author of Les Misérables, who spent 19 years in exile.
ids.murasaki-shikibu: A lady of the Japanese court who wrote what may be the world's first novel.
ids.rumi: The scholar turned mystic poet whose verses of love are read around the world.
ids.li-bai: China's best-loved poet, of wine, mountains and the moon.
ids.rabindranath-tagore: The Bengali poet who was the first non-European Nobel winner, and wrote two national anthems.
ids.shah-jahan: The Mughal emperor who built the Taj Mahal for the wife he loved.
ids.moses: The prophet who, in the Bible's story, led his people out of slavery in Egypt.
ids.laozi: The old master of the Way, who wrote a little book and rode off into the west.
ids.sun-tzu: The general whose Art of War is still read by soldiers, coaches and business leaders.
ids.saint-peter: The fisherman Jesus called "the rock", remembered as the first pope.
ids.thomas-aquinas: The "Dumb Ox" who became the greatest thinker of medieval Europe.
ids.francis-of-assisi: The rich young man who gave everything away and preached to the birds.
ids.maimonides: The great Jewish thinker of the Middle Ages, and doctor at the court of Saladin.
ids.niccolo-machiavelli: The Florentine who wrote The Prince, a ruthless rulebook for rulers.
ids.john-calvin: The reformer who made Geneva a Protestant city and inspired churches worldwide.
ids.guru-nanak: The founder of Sikhism, who taught one God and the equality of all people.
ids.john-locke: The philosopher of liberty, whose ideas ended up in the American Declaration of Independence.
ids.voltaire: The witty voice of the Enlightenment, who fought for free speech and tolerance.
ids.jean-jacques-rousseau: The philosopher who wrote "Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains".
ids.adam-smith: The absent-minded Scot who explained how markets work.
ids.immanuel-kant: The philosopher of Königsberg who asked what we can know and how we should act.
ids.mother-teresa: The nun who spent her life caring for the poorest of the poor in Calcutta.
ids.zhang-qian: The envoy who walked into the unknown west and opened the way for the Silk Road.
ids.xuanzang: The monk who walked from China to India and back to find the true teachings of the Buddha.
ids.leif-erikson: The Norse explorer who reached America about 500 years before Columbus.
ids.henry-the-navigator: The prince who sent Portugal's ships into the unknown Atlantic.
ids.francis-drake: The sea dog who sailed around the world: a hero in England, a pirate in Spain.
ids.roald-amundsen: The Norwegian who was first to the South Pole and first through the Northwest Passage.
ids.khufu: The pharaoh behind the Great Pyramid, the last Wonder of the Ancient World still standing.
ids.hatshepsut: The queen who made herself pharaoh, and the stepson who tried to erase her from history.
ids.tutankhamun: A boy pharaoh who ruled briefly, and whose untouched tomb made him the most famous of them all.
ids.leonidas-i: The Spartan king who held the pass at Thermopylae with 300 men.
ids.spartacus: The gladiator who led a slave army against Rome.
ids.boudica: The warrior queen of Britain who burned Roman London.
ids.wu-zetian: The only woman ever to rule China as emperor in her own name.
ids.harun-al-rashid: The caliph of Baghdad at its height, and hero of the Thousand and One Nights.
ids.sejong-the-great: The scholar king who gave Korea its own alphabet.
ids.pachacuti: The Inca ruler who "shook the earth", built an empire and Machu Picchu.
ids.moctezuma-ii: The last great ruler of the Aztecs, who welcomed Cortés into his city.
ids.tokugawa-ieyasu: The patient warlord who unified Japan and began 250 years of peace.
ids.vlad-the-impaler: The prince of Wallachia whose cruelty gave the world Dracula.
ids.toussaint-louverture: Born enslaved, he led the revolt that created Haiti, the first free Black republic.
ids.thomas-jefferson: He wrote "all men are created equal" and doubled the size of the United States.
ids.frederick-douglass: He escaped slavery and became its most powerful enemy, with his voice and his pen.
ids.harriet-tubman: She escaped slavery, then went back again and again to lead others to freedom.
ids.emperor-meiji: The emperor under whom Japan went from samurai to steamships in one lifetime.
ids.charles-de-gaulle: The general who led Free France in the Second World War and founded the Fifth Republic.
